name: Fante
notes: Fante (Fanti, Mfantse), the coastal Akan literary standard of the Central and Western Regions of Ghana. Inherits the shared Akan vowel/consonant/digraph inventory from `ak` (Asante Twi standard) via `graphemes_base`/`allophones_base`/`positional_graphemes_base`, overriding the points where Fante diverges: (1) NINE oral vowels, adding ɪ ʊ (the −RTR reflexes of e/o, distinctly written in Fante where Asante Twi leaves them as unwritten allophones of ⟨e⟩/⟨o⟩) alongside a e ɛ i o ɔ u; (2) Fante is the only Twi-Fante variety with an alveolar affricate contrast /ts/ vs /dz/ distinct from plain /t/ /d/, written ⟨ts⟩ and ⟨dz⟩ (also spelled with the single letter ⟨z⟩, which is why Fante is the only variety whose alphabet includes ⟨z⟩); (3) the labialised digraphs ⟨tw dw hw⟩, which in Asante Twi spell the labialised velars /kʷ ɡʷ hʷ/ (orthographic variants of ⟨kw gw hw⟩), instead spell the labial-palatalised affricates/fricative /tɕʷ dʑʷ ɕʷ/ in Fante — the palatalised counterparts of ⟨ky gy hy⟩ /tɕ dʑ ɕ/, which Fante shares unchanged with Asante Twi. TONE: as in Akan generally, tone (high/low with downstep) is not marked in the standard orthography and is not modelled here.

ancestors.notes: Fante is a variety of Akan; shares the bulk of the grapheme inventory with the Asante-based `ak` spec, diverging in the affricate series and two extra vowel letters.

location.notes: Central Region, Ghana — the Fante-speaking heartland around Cape Coast.
